html:
The Permians are the peoples who speak the Permic languages, a branch of the Uralic family: the Komi and the Udmurts. The map shows them around 800 across the forests of northeast European Russia, west of the Urals.

They lived by hunting, fishing, trapping and some farming. Their furs were in demand, and they traded them south to the Volga Bulgars and west to Novgorod, which took fur tribute from the northern forests.

In 1372 the Russian monk Stephen of Perm began to preach to the Komi and made an alphabet for their language, the Old Permic script. In 1472 Moscow annexed the land of Great Perm. Udmurtia and the Komi Republic are now republics of Russia.
